{"type": "fix", "title": "fix(docfix-poll): reap zero-own-commit wedged branches cleanup skips", "commit_subject": "fix(docfix-poll): ancestor check + wt-remove fallback in salvage_wedged", "summary_md": "## Summary\n- A run that dies before its first commit leaves a branch whose tip is already on `origin/master`. `bin/cleanup` skips it as "not merged" (exit 0, ref survives), so `salvage_wedged_branch` could never reap it and the branch re-alerted every night.\n- Added a `merge-base --is-ancestor` guard: if the branch tip is already on `origin/master` and the tree is clean, `wt-remove --force --volumes` + `branch -D` remove it directly.\n- Branches with their own commits (not ancestors of `origin/master`) fall through to the existing "leaving" path — nothing unique is lost.\n- Same gap exists after a successful salvage push: `bin/cleanup` skips the branch (the salvage commit is on no merged PR), so the ref survived and re-wedged the next night. After a successful push, the code now removes the worktree and ref itself if `cleanup` leaves them behind.\n- Tests 23a/23b/23c cover all three cases; a `wt-remove` stub and `show-ref`/`merge-base` shim exit codes were added to the sandbox."}
